pretreatments.description: Ensilage of giant reed involves wet storage with microbial fermentation. Giant reed was supplemented with water to reach a total solids (TS) content of around 40% and packed into 1-gallon-size zipper bags. The bags were vacuumed to minimize oxygen presence. Ensilage was conducted in triplicate for each harvest date. After 60 days of ensilage, samples were mixed thoroughly. The remaining silage samples were stored at -20 °C for subsequent anaerobic digestion (AD) and enzymatic hydrolysis tests. Volatile compounds were measured by correcting TS based on lactic acid (0.375), total VFAs (0.892), and ethanol (1.000) content to calculate corrected TS and VS.

Fungal pretreatment of giant reed involved inoculation with *C. subvermispora* (ATCC 96608) prepared from 2% malt extract agar at 28 °C for 7 days. The liquid inoculum was prepared in 50 mL 2% malt extract liquid medium in 500-mL Erlenmeyer flasks. Flasks were sealed, statically cultivated at 28 °C for 7 days. Mycelia were transferred, washed with sterilized deionized (DI) water, suspended in 200 mL sterilized DI water, and homogenized. Twelve 1-L bottles containing giant reed were loaded and autoclaved at 121 °C for 30 min. After cooling, bottles were inoculated with homogenized liquid mycelia (16 mL each) and supplemented with DI water to obtain final moisture content of around 70%. Bottles were incubated at 28 ± 1 °C for 30 days. Remaining mixture was dried at 40 °C for about 2 days to reach moisture content lower than 10%.
